title: New mRNA Vaccine Offers Hope for Skin Cancer Patients
subtitle: Recent clinical trials show promising results for a personalized treatment against high-risk melanoma.

summary.en: Pharmaceutical companies Moderna and Merck have announced positive results from a major clinical trial for a new skin cancer vaccine. The treatment uses mRNA technology to help the human immune system recognize and fight cancer cells. This vaccine is designed specifically for patients with high-risk melanoma, a serious form of skin cancer. Experts believe this personalized approach could change how we treat cancer in the future. Public health officials are now discussing the potential impact of this medical breakthrough.
summary.zh: 製藥公司莫德納與默克宣布，一款新型皮膚癌疫苗的大型臨床試驗取得了正面成果。該療法運用信使核糖核酸技術，協助人體免疫系統辨識並對抗癌細胞。此疫苗專為高風險黑色素瘤患者設計，這是一種嚴重的皮膚癌。專家認為，這種個人化的治療方式可能改變未來的癌症治療模式。公共衛生官員目前正討論這項醫學突破的潛在影響。

paragraphs.en: A major breakthrough in medical science has brought new hope to patients fighting skin cancer. Pharmaceutical companies Moderna and Merck recently announced successful results from a large Phase 3 clinical trial for a new vaccine. A Phase 3 trial is the final and most important stage of testing a new medicine before it can be approved for general use. This new treatment is designed to help the body’s immune system identify and attack cancer cells more effectively.
paragraphs.zh: 醫學界的一項重大突破為對抗皮膚癌的患者帶來了新希望。製藥公司莫德納 (Moderna) 與默克 (Merck) 近期宣布，針對一款新型疫苗的大型第三期臨床試驗取得了成功。第三期試驗是新藥在獲准全面使用前，最後且最重要的測試階段。這項新療法旨在協助人體免疫系統更有效地辨識並攻擊癌細胞。

paragraphs.en: The vaccine uses mRNA technology, which is the same type of technology used in some COVID-19 vaccines. In this case, the vaccine is personalized, meaning it is created specifically for each individual patient. It is intended for people with high-risk melanoma, which is a dangerous type of skin cancer that can spread quickly to other parts of the body. By training the immune system to recognize the unique features of a patient's cancer, the vaccine aims to prevent the disease from returning after surgery.
paragraphs.zh: 該疫苗採用信使核糖核酸技術，這與部分新冠肺炎疫苗所使用的技術相同。在此案例中，疫苗是個人化的，意即它是為每位患者量身打造的。其適用對象為高風險黑色素瘤患者，這是一種危險的皮膚癌，能迅速擴散至身體其他部位。透過訓練免疫系統辨識患者癌細胞的獨特特徵，該疫苗旨在預防癌症在手術後復發。

paragraphs.en: According to KFF Health News, this development is a significant step forward in cancer research. Céline Gounder, an editor-at-large for public health at KFF Health News, discussed the potential of this vaccine on CBS News 24/7’s The Daily Report on August 19. Gounder, who is a former melanoma patient herself, highlighted how this technology could change the way doctors treat high-risk cases. The excitement surrounding these results comes after years of research into how mRNA can be used to teach the body to fight diseases beyond just viruses.
paragraphs.zh: 根據凱澤家庭基金會健康新聞 (KFF Health News) 的報導，這項進展是癌症研究的一大躍進。該媒體的公共衛生特約編輯席琳·岡德 (Céline Gounder) 於 8 月 19 日在哥倫比亞廣播公司新聞網 (CBS News) 的節目《每日報導》中，討論了這款疫苗的潛力。身為前黑色素瘤患者的岡德強調，這項技術可能改變醫師治療高風險病例的方式。這些成果之所以令人振奮，是因為多年來研究人員一直在探討如何運用信使核糖核酸技術，教導人體對抗病毒以外的疾病。

paragraphs.en: While the results are very positive, experts note that this is still a new area of medicine. The primary goal of the vaccine is to stop the cancer from coming back in patients who have already had their tumors removed. Because the vaccine is personalized, it requires a complex process to create a treatment that matches the specific biology of each patient’s tumor. This makes the process more difficult and expensive than producing standard vaccines, but researchers believe the health benefits for patients are worth the effort.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管結果非常正面，專家仍指出這在醫學領域尚屬新興範疇。該疫苗的主要目標是防止已切除腫瘤的患者癌症復發。由於疫苗是個人化的，因此需要複雜的程序來製作出符合每位患者腫瘤特定生物特徵的療法。這使得製作過程比生產標準疫苗更困難且昂貴，但研究人員認為，對患者帶來的健康益處值得投入這些努力。

paragraphs.en: The medical community is watching these developments closely. If the vaccine continues to show success, it could lead to a new way of treating other types of cancer as well. Scientists are already looking at how this technology might be applied to different forms of the disease. The ability to create a treatment that is custom-made for a patient's own immune system could be the future of cancer care.
paragraphs.zh: 醫學界正密切關注這些發展。若該疫苗持續展現成效，或許能引領出治療其他癌症的新途徑。科學家已在研究如何將此技術應用於不同形式的癌症。這種能為患者自身免疫系統量身打造療法的能力，可能成為未來癌症照護的趨勢。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the science, there are also discussions about how such advanced treatments will be made available to the public. As with any new and expensive medical technology, health officials will need to consider how to ensure that patients can access these vaccines. KFF Health News has been reporting on various health issues, including the importance of finding affordable care. As this vaccine moves closer to potential approval, the focus will likely shift toward how it can be distributed safely and fairly to those who need it most.
paragraphs.zh: 除了科學層面，各界也針對如何讓大眾取得這類先進療法進行討論。如同任何昂貴的新興醫療技術，衛生官員將需要考量如何確保患者能獲得這些疫苗。凱澤家庭基金會健康新聞持續報導各類健康議題，包括尋求可負擔醫療的重要性。隨著該疫苗距離獲准使用更進一步，焦點可能會轉向如何安全且公平地將其分配給最需要的族群。

paragraphs.en: For now, the results from the Moderna and Merck trial provide a clear sign of progress. Patients with high-risk melanoma often face a very uncertain future, and this vaccine offers a new tool to help them stay healthy. While more testing and regulatory reviews are still needed before the vaccine is widely available, the medical community remains optimistic. This breakthrough demonstrates how quickly science is moving to solve some of the most difficult health challenges of our time.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，莫德納與默克的試驗結果提供了明確的進步跡象。高風險黑色素瘤患者往往面臨極不確定的未來，而這款疫苗提供了一項協助他們保持健康的新工具。雖然在疫苗廣泛普及前仍需更多測試與監管審查，醫學界仍保持樂觀。這項突破展現了科學正以多快的速度，致力於解決當代最艱鉅的健康挑戰。

paragraphs.en: In the coming months, more data from the trial will likely be shared with the public and other medical experts. This will help doctors better understand how long the protection lasts and which patients will benefit the most from the treatment. For many, this represents a major shift in the fight against cancer, moving from general treatments to ones that are designed for the individual. As researchers continue their work, the hope is that this mRNA vaccine will become a standard part of cancer care, saving lives and providing a stronger defense against one of the world’s most serious diseases.
paragraphs.zh: 在未來幾個月內，更多試驗數據可能會與大眾及其他醫學專家分享。這將有助於醫師更深入了解保護效力能持續多久，以及哪些患者能從中獲得最大助益。對許多人而言，這代表了抗癌方式的重大轉變，從通用療法轉向為個人量身設計的治療。隨著研究人員持續努力，各界期望這款信使核糖核酸疫苗能成為癌症照護的標準配備，不僅能拯救生命，更能針對全球最嚴重的疾病之一提供更強大的防禦。

keyTerms.definitionEn: An important discovery or event that helps to improve a situation or provide an answer to a problem.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此詞常被誤認為僅指物理上的「打破」，但在醫學或科學領域指重大的研究進展。文中：A major breakthrough in medical science has brought new hope to patients fighting skin cancer.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A senior journalist or editor who does not have a specific desk or department but covers a wide range of topics.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 特約編輯；總編輯（不隸屬於特定部門）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此職稱容易讓人困惑，at-large 在此指「不限於特定職責範圍」。文中：Céline Gounder, an editor-at-large for public health at KFF Health News, discussed the potential of this vaccine on CBS News 24/7’s The Daily Report on August 19.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To change the focus, direction, or position of something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（輪班），這裡作動詞，指關注點的轉移。文中：As this vaccine moves closer to potential approval, the focus will likely shift toward how it can be distributed safely and fairly to those who need it most.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of the new mRNA vaccine according to the text?

options.A: To replace surgery as the first line of treatment for skin cancer.
options.B: To prevent the recurrence of cancer in patients who have already undergone surgery.
options.C: To cure patients who have advanced, spreading melanoma that cannot be operated on.
options.D: To serve as a standard, mass-produced vaccine for anyone at risk of skin cancer.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段與第四段，疫苗的目的是在手術後訓練免疫系統，防止癌症復發（prevent the disease from returning after surgery）。選項 A 錯誤，因為疫苗是輔助手術後的治療，而非取代手術；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章強調是針對已移除腫瘤的患者；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章明確指出該疫苗是「個人化」的，並非通用的大規模生產疫苗。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might this vaccine be more difficult to implement than traditional vaccines?

options.A: The mRNA technology used is still considered experimental and unsafe for most people.
options.B: It requires a complex, individualized manufacturing process for every single patient.
options.C: Medical experts are still debating whether the vaccine is effective against viruses.
options.D: Pharmaceutical companies are currently unwilling to invest in the necessary technology.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，因為疫苗是「個人化」（personalized）的，必須針對每位患者腫瘤的特定生物學特徵進行匹配，這使得製造過程比標準疫苗更複雜且昂貴。選項 A 不正確，因為文章提到試驗結果是正面的；選項 C 與文章提到的疫苗用途（癌症治療）無關；選項 D 與文章內容矛盾，因為 Moderna 和 Merck 已經在進行大規模臨床試驗。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'a major shift' mean in the context of cancer care?

options.A: A sudden decrease in the total number of cancer patients.
options.B: A fundamental change in the approach from general treatments to personalized ones.
options.C: A physical movement of medical equipment to different hospitals.
options.D: A temporary pause in research to evaluate new trial data.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章最後一段提到「moving from general treatments to ones that are designed for the individual」，這正是「major shift」所指的轉變。選項 A 錯誤，文章並未提及患者人數減少；選項 C 將 shift 理解為物理移動，不符合語境；選項 D 錯誤，因為研究並未暫停，反而在持續進行中。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the new mRNA vaccine?

options.A: The vaccine is a guaranteed cure for all types of skin cancer.
options.B: Public health officials have already approved the vaccine for immediate distribution.
options.C: While promising, the vaccine faces challenges regarding cost and accessibility despite its potential.
options.D: The vaccine is primarily a business success for Moderna and Merck rather than a medical one.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章整體在討論該疫苗作為癌症治療的突破性潛力，但也同時在第四段與第六段點出了其複雜的製造過程、高昂成本以及未來分配的挑戰。選項 A 過於誇大，文章僅提到針對高風險黑色素瘤；選項 B 錯誤，文章提到仍需更多測試與監管審查；選項 D 錯誤，文章重點在於醫療科學的進步，而非商業獲利。
